classification: SYNTHETIC seed facts plus explicit demo assumptions; no measured demand
objective: Produce one useful local artifact while favoring learning and cross-venture reuse, discounted by subjective seed confidence; do not maximize revenue or utilization.
estimatePolicy: Delivery and test-preparation minutes are new, unmeasured estimates for narrower demo offerings, not proportional reductions of seed hours. Learning, reuse and confidence are inherited from each named seed direction as a contestable assumption. Future consented observation and recruitment are not included in this week's plans-only allocation.

ventures.name: Ledgerleaf Tools
ventures.estimateReason: One strict CSV parser, a small finding contract and a local report; no import integrations, repairs, accounting or downstream export product.
ventures.smallestOffer: A local CSV preflight with record, line and column findings; paste or select a UTF-8 file and download a value-free JSON report.
ventures.nonGoals: No accounting certification, bookkeeping, file repair, formula execution, real financial-file exercise, signing, billing or production integration.

dependency.label: A fictional CSV fixture and a stable record/code contract
dependency.basis: Seed fixture is available; the original checker in this demo has automated artifact tests. Neither establishes demand.

plan.audienceHypothesis: People preparing a small CSV import; no such people have been recruited.
plan.question: Will a prospective user choose this checker over manual inspection for a second fictional import?
plan.protocol: After separate owner approval and consent, offer three prospective users a five-record fictional CSV and the checker. Ask each to explain a duplicate finding without coaching, then let them choose checker or plain text for a second sample.
plan.pass: At least 2 of 3 choose the checker again AND correctly identify the duplicate within five minutes.
plan.stop: Park or simplify if fewer than 2 of 3 meet both conditions, or if explaining the checker takes longer than manual inspection.
plan.interpretation: A tiny convenience sample could disconfirm utility; even a pass is not paying demand, retention or product-market fit.

ventures.reuseUse: Own the value-free finding schema, parser, fixture patterns and offline report UI.
ventures.reuseBoundary: The other ventures can reuse components, not inherit evidence of customer demand.

uncertainties.disconfirm: Reader cannot explain the duplicate-key finding

uncertainties.claim: JSON findings can support a later UI
uncertainties.disconfirm: Finding lacks a stable row and code

ventures.name: Fieldnote Guides
ventures.offerHypothesis: Make a supply-drawer reset easier to start
ventures.estimateReason: One page using 12 index cards, 3 binder clips, 2 empty envelopes and removable labels, with an undo step; no catalog or physical observation.
ventures.smallestOffer: A printable count, group, label, return and undo guide for a fictional supply drawer.
ventures.nonGoals: No repair, equipment maintenance, electrical, chemical or safety instructions; no physical intervention.

dependency.label: Fictional inventory and a one-page comprehension rubric
dependency.basis: The seed supplies the inventory. The proposed guide and rubric remain unbuilt.

plan.audienceHypothesis: People who postpone organizing a shared supply drawer; unmeasured.
plan.question: Does someone choose and start using the guide instead of a plain list?
plan.protocol: With later owner approval and consent, offer three people a fictional inventory, a plain list and the guide. Ask them to pick a format and state their first grouping and reversal step in five minutes.
plan.pass: At least 2 of 3 choose the guide and can state a first action and how to undo it without another page.
plan.stop: Park if fewer than 2 of 3 meet the rule, or setup takes more work than the plain list.
plan.interpretation: Format choice and comprehension are weak utility signals, not purchases.

ventures.reuseUse: Use CSV checks for a fictional drawer-inventory table; reuse printable finding labels and the pass/stop test template.
ventures.reuseBoundary: A CSV parser does not write a useful guide; the original page and comprehension work are still needed.

uncertainties.claim: A guide helps people start organizing
uncertainties.disconfirm: Guide requires more setup than a plain list
Reader needs an unexplained second page

ventures.name: Quietbench Templates
ventures.offerHypothesis: Make purchasing requests easier to understand
ventures.estimateReason: One request form with required/optional labels, a keyboard pass and print reading order; not a three-template catalog or accessibility certification.
ventures.smallestOffer: A printable purchasing request with item, reason, alternatives, hypothetical cost, needed-by window and reviewer question.
ventures.nonGoals: No accessibility certification, procurement workflow, employer adoption, approval authority or real purchasing.

dependency.label: Plain-language field order and a keyboard/print review plan
dependency.basis: The seed lists fields. A review plan can be drafted locally; the form and human review remain unperformed.

plan.audienceHypothesis: People drafting small purchasing requests; unmeasured.
plan.question: Would a drafter choose this form over a blank note for a second fictional request?
plan.protocol: After approval and consent, ask three prospective drafters to navigate a fictional request using only a keyboard, explain which purpose field is required, then choose form or note for another request.
plan.pass: At least 2 of 3 finish without coaching, identify required purpose and choose the form again; no keyboard blocker is acceptable.
plan.stop: Revise for any keyboard blocker; otherwise park if fewer than 2 of 3 meet the rule.
plan.interpretation: A small walkthrough is neither an accessibility audit nor adoption evidence.

ventures.reuseUse: Reuse labeled controls, text-only finding codes and required-column checks on fictional request exports.
ventures.reuseBoundary: The checker cannot certify accessibility or whether a purchasing request is justified.

uncertainties.disconfirm: Required purpose is unclear without visual layout
Keyboard traversal differs from reading order

ventures.name: Routepaper Planners
ventures.estimateReason: One category/time-window/can-wait/done sheet for a library return, labels and a fictional tote drop; no navigation or interviews.
ventures.smallestOffer: A printable, location-free category grouping sheet for three fictional errands.
ventures.nonGoals: No addresses, location histories, travel predictions, real schedules or navigation.

dependency.label: Fictional errands and an address-free grouping rule
dependency.basis: Seed examples exist. The sheet is only a proposed alternative in this demo.

plan.audienceHypothesis: People planning errands who do not need maps; unmeasured.
plan.question: Will someone choose the grouped sheet over a plain list, and does it change a decision?
plan.protocol: After approval and consent, give three people the same fictional errands in plain-list and grouped-sheet versions. Ask them to choose one and explain a grouping or deferral decision without adding any addresses.
plan.pass: At least 2 of 3 choose the sheet and identify one changed planning decision, without requesting locations.
plan.stop: Park if grouping changes no decision, takes more effort than a list, or requires addresses.
plan.interpretation: This is a low-scope interest test, not proof of repeat use or sales.

ventures.reuseUse: Reuse the local-file pattern and required-column checks for category, time-window, can-wait and done.
ventures.reuseBoundary: Do not introduce location collection just because the parser accepts arbitrary text.

uncertainties.claim: Category grouping is useful without maps
A useful sheet needs no addresses

ventures.name: Tinylesson Studio
ventures.estimateReason: One six-minute lesson, three fictional names and a transfer answer rubric; no course platform or observed learning gains.
ventures.smallestOffer: An offline lesson on stable purpose and sortable dates, followed by an unrelated file-naming exercise.
ventures.nonGoals: No access to personal files, course platform, learning-improvement claim or certification.

dependency.label: Original sample names and a transfer-scoring rubric
dependency.basis: Seed naming examples exist. The lesson and transfer exercise remain proposed.

plan.audienceHypothesis: People uncertain about file naming; unmeasured.
plan.question: Will a learner choose another short exercise after independently transferring the idea?
plan.protocol: After approval and consent, give three people a six-minute lesson using fictional filenames, then an unrelated naming exercise with a purpose/date rubric. Offer another exercise or an exit.
plan.pass: At least 2 of 3 meet the purpose/date rubric on the new example without copying and voluntarily choose another exercise.
plan.stop: Park if fewer than 2 of 3 meet both conditions, copying substitutes for transfer, or exercise and feedback exceed six minutes.
plan.interpretation: No causal learning gain or willingness to pay can be inferred from this tiny test.

ventures.reuseUse: Turn fictional CSV failures into original data-hygiene exercises with stable, machine-checkable finding codes.
ventures.reuseBoundary: Automated check results are answer rubrics, not evidence that a learner improved.

uncertainties.disconfirm: Learner only copies the sample naming pattern

uncertainties.claim: Six minutes can fit one objective
uncertainties.disconfirm: Exercise and feedback exceed the timebox
